subject: Public-facing subprocessor snapshot & short explainers for hosted API console
messages:
From: Mary Jones <mary.jones@acme.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Procurement <procure@acme.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick Q: subprocessor list + residency language for hosted API

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Acme's integration team is aligned and Procurement asked me to follow up on two items before we move to legal:

1) Can you provide a short, customer-facing snapshot of the subprocessors that handle hosted API telemetry/metrics, logs, and object storage? They want an easy list to include in our procurement packet.

2) We need plain-language copy for the console (hover/help text) that makes it clear whether request payloads or generated outputs may cross international borders. Simple phrasing preferred — our security reviewers are not deep into infra details.

If you can send something by EOD Wednesday that would help keep our review on schedule.

Thanks,
Mary
Mary Jones
Senior IT Procurement, Acme Corp
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Mary Jones <mary.jones@acme.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick Q: subprocessor list + residency language for hosted API

Hi Mary — thanks for the clear ask. Looping in Karthik (privacy/legal lens) and Avery (console copy/UX).

Attached is a short subprocessor snapshot (DPA_subprocessors_snapshot_v2.docx) that separates categories we typically publish: 
- Telemetry & analytics (aggregated metrics only)
- Metrics/log storage (time-limited logs used for debugging and SLOs)
- Object storage (customer assets, only if uploaded by customer and per settings)

For the console help text, we propose a 1–2 sentence explainer and a tooltip variant:

Console short: "Data sent to the Hosted API may be processed in multiple regions to provide the best performance; you can view and request controls for where data is stored and how long logs are retained in Settings."

Tooltip (hover): "We route requests to nearby regions for latency. Sensitive data residency controls are available under Settings > Data residency — contact your Account Manager for a dedicated region or Private deployment options."

We included two examples in console_snippet_examples.md (one sales-friendly, one more technical).

Next steps: Karthik — any legal/accuracy redlines? Avery — can you mock the residency toggle (screenshot attached) and propose copy that fits a single-line help pill?

Best,
Laura Bennett
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2027 09:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick Q: subprocessor list + residency language for hosted API

Thanks — I reviewed the snapshot and the proposed console lines. A couple of legal notes and suggested edits for publishable language: 

1) Avoid the phrase 'may be processed' without clarifying the triggers — use 'typically processed' or 'routed' and add a parenthetical that gives the customer a control path. E.g., replace the first sentence with: "We route API requests to the closest available region to reduce latency; customers can request controls for storage location and log retention in Settings."

2) For subprocessors, list vendors by category and add an expiry/last-updated date on the console card — customers expect a timestamp.

3) Remove any implied promise about 'never leaving the US' — instead, provide the residency controls and a clear path to Private deployments for strict requirements.

Attached: quick redline suggestions in console_snippet_examples.md. Happy to sign off after the small edits.

-karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Mary Jones <mary.jones@acme.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Procurement <procure@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Jul 2027 14:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick Q: subprocessor list + residency language for hosted API

Laura — this is very helpful. A couple of clarifying asks from Procurement: 

• Can the subprocessor snapshot include the date it was last validated (so we can show it to our internal legal)?
• For the console card, Procurement prefers the sales-friendly short line but asks for a 'what this means' expand link that shows a one-paragraph technical note (we can include that in our packet).

Also, will you be able to include a DocuSign-ready clause for the DPA (we have a template that needs a short vendor-supplied paragraph about subprocessors/data residency)? If you can provide that by Friday it would keep our timeline intact.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Mary
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Jul 2027 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick Q: subprocessor list + residency language for hosted API

Hi Mary — good questions. Short summary of what we're delivering today and immediate next steps: 

Delivered (attachments + links):
- DPA_subprocessors_snapshot_v2.docx — includes per-category vendor list and a "last validated" field (2027-07-15).
- console_snippet_examples.md — updated with Karthik's legal edits and two variants (short + expand paragraph).
- residency_toggle_mockup.png — single-line mock for Settings > Data residency.

DocuSign clause: Karthik drafted a concise paragraph we can paste into your DPA template: "Redwood Inference engages subprocessors to provide hosting, telemetry, and support services. A current list of subprocessors (by category) and the date of last validation is maintained in the Redwood Console. Customers may request evidence of subprocessor contracts and controls; additional residency or private deployment options are available under Redwood's enterprise offerings."

Next steps: 
- I'll upload the snapshot to the shared Drive link and ping Procurement (HubSpot: 1234567).
- Avery will post the single-line help pill in the console QA build and share a screenshot for your review early next week.
- Karthik will prepare the short DocuSign paragraph in plain text for your legal team.

If you'd like, we can do a 20-min sync on Monday to walk through the console mock and the DPA clause. Proposed time: Mon 9am PT. Let me know if that works.

Best regards,
Laura Bennett
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
